newsitem.title: ISRAEL: RESEARCH ALERT - Makhteshim estimates up.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Makhteshim estimates up.

text.p: Salomon Brothers raised its 1997 net income and revenue estimates for Makhteshim Chemical Works Ltd, citing a more aggressive 1997 outlook for the Israeli maker of generic agrochemicals.
Makhteshim's 1996 results exceeded expectations, analyst Victor Halpert said in a report provided to Reuters on Sunday.

"As a result of a more aggressive 1997 outlook we are upgrading our net income estimates from $35.2 million to $35.9 million. Due to the fast pace of expansions in Latin America in 1996 we are increasing our 1997 revenue projections from $576 million to $688.8 million," the report said.
The company had net income of $30.4 million and revenue of $547.2 million in 1996. Latin America provided the fastest growth during 1996, as year-to-year sales in the region rose 52 percent.
Salomon Brothers estimates Makhteshim will earn $0.48 a share in 1998, up from an estimated $0.40 in 1997. Sales will rise 10.6 percent in 1998 to $761.5 million, Halpert forecast.

"We are reiterating our strong buy recommendation on the shares of Makhteshim as the company is continuing to achieve its milestones," the report said. "Our 12-month price target is 24-26 shekels or about 16 times our 1998 earnings per share estimate."
Makhteshim is currently at 21.43 shekels a share. The company is a subsidiary of Koor Industries Ltd.
